title: The Ājurrūmiyya and its place
summary: A few pages that set out iʿrāb: the most memorised first book of naḥw, from the Maghrib to Indonesia.

sections.heading: The book
paragraphs: Al-Muqaddima al-Ājurrūmiyya opens with the definition of speech and the three kinds of word, then gives iʿrāb, its four states and their signs, and the words that are marfūʿ, manṣūb and makhfūḍ. It is short enough to be learnt by heart in weeks.
More than sixty commentaries were written on it. It reached Europe in the sixteenth century and was printed with an English translation in Cambridge in 1852.

sections.heading: Where it is read
paragraphs: Al-Ājurrūmiyya is the first book of naḥw in the Arab world and the Maghrib, and in the pesantren of Indonesia as Jurumiyah. In the West it is often the first classical text an English-speaking student meets.
